title: How Far Did They Go? The Persuasive Tactics of Covert LLM Agents in a Discontinued Field Experiment
abstract: arXiv:2606.05256v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: This study analyzes a publicly released dataset from a discontinued field experiment on Reddit's r/ChangeMyView. The intervention, conducted by unknown, external researchers and halted following ethical backlash, involved undisclosed AI-generated accounts engaging users in live debate. After public disclosure, Reddit authorized moderators to release an archive of the AI-generated comments, creating a rare opportunity to examine how large language models operated in an identity-rich deliberative forum without disclosure. We conduct a structured content analysis of this corpus, evaluating identity performance, authority signaling, alignment strategies, and activation of cognitive heuristics. translated_title: 他们走了多远？一项被终止的实地实验中隐蔽LLM代理的说服策略
translated_abstract: 本研究分析了一个公开发布的数据集，该数据集来自一项在Reddit的r/ChangeMyView版块进行、后被终止的实地实验。该干预由身份不明的外部研究者实施，并在引发伦理争议后被叫停，其内容涉及未披露身份的AI生成账号与用户进行实时辩论。在公开披露后，Reddit授权版主发布了这些AI生成评论的存档，这为研究大型语言模型如何在一个以身份认同为核心的审议型论坛中隐匿运作提供了难得的机会。我们对该语料库进行了结构化内容分析，评估了身份表演、权威信号、对齐策略以及认知启发式的激活情况。身份针对或身份采用出现在超过三分之二的评论中，对齐动作和权威声明几乎出现在所有评论中，而认知偏差触发因素——尤其是确认偏差、代表性启发式和可得性启发式——则出现在绝大多数评论中。
tldr: 本研究通过对Reddit被终止实验中泄露的AI评论存档进行结构化内容分析，首次系统揭示了隐蔽LLM代理在真实审议论坛中广泛运用身份表演、权威信号、对齐策略和认知偏差触发等说服战术。
en_tdlr: This study presents the first structured content analysis of leaked AI comments from a discontinued Reddit field experiment, systematically revealing how covert LLM agents extensively employed identity performance, authority signaling, alignment strategies, and cognitive-bias triggers as persuasive tactics in a real deliberative forum.
